title: feat(safenet): surface the check as an audit-log step with attestation link
description:
## What it solves

Resolves: the first visible surface of the Safenet checks integration (PRD
history design) — the read layer merged in #8424/#8448/#8469/#8482/#8483 had
no UI. A transaction's audit log now shows whether Safenet checked it and
with what verdict.

## How this PR fixes it

`SafenetAuditRow` renders the check as an audit-log step — Simulating / No
issues found / Risk detected · By Safenet — between the signatures and the
execution row. Labels and copy follow the PRD states table.

- Renders nothing until a check has been observed for the hash: most
  transactions never had one, so an UNAVAILABLE row per transaction would be
  noise. No skeleton; an entrance animation softens the late insert.
- "Safenet" in the actor line is the proof link, shown only on "No issues
  found": BENIGN is underivable without a FROST-verified attestation, so the
  label and the link always travel together. It targets the attestation
  transaction on the Safenet chain's block explorer, falling back to the
  Safenet explorer's `/#/safeTx` hash route when the chain config is
  unavailable.
- Status colors apply in dark mode only; in light mode every icon uses the
  sibling rows' default color and the severity signal is the label.
- The step is dated from the attested block on the Safenet chain (one header
  read per settled check; null never suppresses a verdict). The row keeps its
  lifecycle position, so its date can read later than Executed below it — the
  attestation settles on another chain and the column reports the truth.

Gating: the CGW `SAFENET_CHECKS` flag (new `FEATURES` entry), loaded lazily
through the feature registry so disabled sessions pay no bundle cost. The
registry stubs the row to null while the flag is off — TxSigners mounts it
bare. TxSigners also subscribes to the same check cache entry so the sibling
rows' `isLast` accounts for the Safenet step (one chain read, shared).

## How to test it

Branch preview (staging CGW serves the flag for chain 1, no env override
needed):
`/transactions/tx?safe=eth:0xF89f49e21A2Bd1fb24332462cB21dc1378aA25e1&id=multisig_0xF89f49e21A2Bd1fb24332462cB21dc1378aA25e1_0x10b35caca9bfe3afa5270b7f0c2e3a7501eaf5df8da07d894d022d5be9cb478a`
→ "No issues found · By Safenet · 11:41:00 AM" between Signed and Executed;
the actor link opens the attestation. Nonce 66 of the same Safe is a second
live check. Any tx without a check (e.g. nonce 64) shows no row and stops
polling after one read. Locally: `yarn workspace @safe-global/web dev`, then
enable `SAFENET_CHECKS` in the sidebar's "Feature flags" override panel.

## Affected flows

- Owner opens a transaction's details (history or queue) and reads the audit
  log — a Safenet step appears for checked transactions.

## Blast radius

- `AuditRow` (`components/common/AuditLog`) gains two additive props
  (`actor`, `iconColor`); consumers TxSigners and MsgAuditLog are untouched
  by default values.
- New `FEATURES.SAFENET_CHECKS` entry (utils `chains.ts`) — inert on chains
  whose CGW config does not serve the flag.
- New lazy feature `safenet-checks` in the web feature registry; no bundle
  cost when disabled.
- Chain reads go through the already-merged reader/store/hook (packages
  utils/store) — no RTK endpoint or CGW contract changes.
- Mobile: none. Shared packages were merged earlier; this PR mounts web-only.

## Risks / not checked

- MALICIOUS / TIMED_OUT / SUBMITTED / IN_PROGRESS never observed live (the
  beta settles in ~5 blocks); those renders are pinned by component tests
  only.
- The gnosisscan link path needs a CGW that serves chain-100 config — staging
  does not, so the deployed preview exercises only the explorer fallback
  (gnosisscan path verified locally against prod CGW).
- Checks attested long after submission (outside the aimed read window) read
  UNAVAILABLE by design and render nothing.
- Not tested on mobile (no mobile surface).

## Visual summary

Live on the branch preview against staging CGW (mainnet Safe, real
Gnosis-beta check, FROST-verified client-side):

| light | dark |
| --- | --- |
| ![light](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Fbartoli/42d353ade65f55cd206edf9b79e1572d/raw/light-nonce65.png) | ![dark](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Fbartoli/42d353ade65f55cd206edf9b79e1572d/raw/dark-nonce65.png) |

A second live check in history context (nonce 66, attested ~70s after
execution):

![history](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Fbartoli/42d353ade65f55cd206edf9b79e1572d/raw/history-nonce66.webp)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[CGW SAFENET_CHECKS flag] --> B[lazy feature registry]
  B --> C[SafenetAuditRow]
  C --> D[useSafenetCheck]
  D --> E[RTK query safenetCheckApi]
  E --> F[SafenetReader: aimed getLogs + group key]
  F --> G[client-side FROST verify]
  G --> H[status -> label/icon/link/date]
```

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 (no mobile surface in this PR)
- [x] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 — no
      analytics events added or changed
- [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻
- [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not
      verify 🎯

findings.claim: The isSafenetEnabled check should be moved directly inside the SafenetAuditRow component instead of being handled where it currently is.

useLoadFeature(SafenetChecksFeature) triggers the dynamic import for every rendered TxSigners regardless of whether Safenet is enabled for the chain, causing a wasted network round trip on non-Safenet chains and undermining the claim that disabled sessions incur no bundle cost. The enabled check should be moved inside SafenetAuditRow itself, or the enabled state checked first so useLoadFeature is only invoked conditionally.

There is no Storybook story file for the new SafenetAuditRow component. The row has 5 statuses, linked and unlinked versions, and different colors in dark mode, and a story would be the only place to view all of these variations side by side.
When the block-header read fails, the reader retries each RPC endpoint in turn, which delays the verdict for that poll.
The feature implementation file is named feature.tsx rather than feature.ts as required by the standard feature layout, unlike every other feature in the codebase.

The last signed row and the created row compute isLast as the negation of showExecutionRow, but when the Safenet audit row actually renders after them, both that row and the neighbor end up marked isLast, which drops the vertical connector between them. Because SafenetAuditRow can return null depending on snapshot state, the parent has no way to know in advance whether a real row will follow, so isLast needs to be computed based on whether the Safenet row will actually render, for example by lifting the check up or exposing a small hook.

The component duplicates the API's logic for choosing the attestation event (oracle first, plain as fallback) instead of sharing it with `packages/store/src/safenet/safenetCheckApi.ts`. The code comment claims it links to the same event the API verifies, but nothing enforces that the two implementations stay in sync, so a future change to one side could make the link point to a transaction other than the one actually verified.

The creation and signature rows determine whether they are the last row by checking only `!showExecutionRow`, without checking whether the new Safenet row will also render. For a transaction still collecting signatures that already has a Safenet check, this causes the last signature (or creation) row to be marked last incorrectly, so its connector line is omitted and the Safenet row appears disconnected from the timeline.

The new environment variable NEXT_PUBLIC_SAFENET_EXPLORER_URL, added in packages/utils/src/features/safenet-checks/constants.ts, is missing from .env.example even though every other Safenet variable is documented there.

useChain is called with snapshot's chainId falling back to an empty string before the snapshot existence check, which works today only because useChain('') happens to return undefined, but the intent would be clearer if the empty-string fallback were dropped or the call were gated on the snapshot's chainId actually being present.
Since an earlier line already returns when there is no snapshot, the subsequent optional chaining on snapshot when calling events.find is redundant and can be simplified to a direct property access.
The dark-mode `iconColor` mapping is untested.

The comment describing the block-header read as costing 'one RPC per settled check' is inaccurate: `blockTimeMs` actually runs on every poll that sees an attestation event, including polls every 6 seconds while waiting for verification and every refetch after the 300-second cache expires, so the comment should be corrected or the read limited to only when status is `BENIGN` or `MALICIOUS`.
The isDarkMode branch and its associated color map have no direct test coverage; removing that branch would not cause any test to fail.

This new component lacks a `.stories.tsx` file, which the project's AGENTS.md conventions require for new components; its five statuses and the new `actor`/`iconColor` props on `AuditRow` are consequently only exercised in tests, not visible in Storybook.
Comments here restate the code rather than explain non-obvious reasoning, exceeding the repository's guidance to treat comments as tech debt and use them only when really necessary.

Several comments in this file merely restate what the code already does (e.g. describing the theme-default link color or that a value is null while running) or point to a PRD instead of explaining non-obvious reasoning, which is heavier commenting than the repository's guideline allows.
The JSDoc acknowledges that this row's date can be later than the date on the "Executed" row below it, which is a product-facing inconsistency that needs sign-off from design or product.

The parent component wraps the row in an extra isSafenetEnabled check even though components rendered from a feature handle already return null when the feature is off or not loaded, so the flag is being checked redundantly.

The feature's lazy-loaded interface is placed in types.ts instead of the contract.ts file that the documented feature layout requires, and because ESLint allows outside code to import types.ts, the interface ends up exposed as part of the public types.
Test coverage should be extended with a TxSigners-level assertion verifying that isLast is set correctly on the row above the Safenet row once the isLast propagation issue is fixed.
This env variable and its related logic can be removed since feature flags can now be overridden locally through the UI via the Feature flags entry in the sidebar, added in #8288.

The new actor and iconColor props added to the shared AuditLog component are not directly tested: actor is only covered indirectly through the Safenet tests, and iconColor along with the new showDash behavior are not covered at all.

In light mode, the "Risk detected" and "Safenet check failed" statuses use the same primary color as surrounding rows, so a flagged transaction looks the same as a normal step; only dark mode applies error or warning colors, and nothing cites a design decision authorizing this.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SAFENET_EXPLORER_URL` is read here but is missing from `apps/web/.env.example`, even though the diff documents every other Safenet environment variable there.

The NEXT_PUBLIC_SAFENET_CHECKS_FORCE environment variable duplicates the local feature-flag override UI already added elsewhere, creating two override paths for a single flag, which is a maintenance hazard; the env var and its corresponding process.env branch should be removed.

The new tests only cover the Safenet row alongside a normal execution row and do not cover a transaction still awaiting signatures that also has a Safenet row, which is the exact scenario in which the timeline connector bug occurs.
The isLast prop on this row and the next one needs to be updated now that the Safenet audit row has been added below them.
Comments here restate the code rather than explain non-obvious reasoning, exceeding the repository's guidance to treat comments as tech debt and use them only when really necessary.
